title: Runtime descriptor
description: How the session attaches to one runtime and turns its records into session events. A descriptor matches and copies; it never computes. runtimes/<name>/descriptor.yaml, with fixtures beside it.

version.description: The descriptor format. Forager refuses a version it does not read.

runtime.description: The runtime this describes, as the launch spec sets it: claude, codex.

title.description: The runtime's display name: Claude Code. runtimes.json lists it beside the name.

runtime_version.description: The runtime version the rules were written against and the fixtures recorded from. Reported in run.started; Forager never checks the installed version.

sources.description: How the session attaches. The terminal bytes are always captured and need no source: there is nothing in them to match.

output.description: Structured output on the runtime's standard output, when the session runs on pipes.

format.description: jsonl: one JSON object per line. Lines that are not JSON objects are not records.

hooks.description: Hook calls the runtime makes. The session installs its forwarder as a command hook for each listed event in the settings the launch passes; the forwarder writes what it reads on its standard input to the local socket as one record.

install.description: How the session installs its forwarder, chosen among the ways the binary implements. claude-settings: a command hook per event, added to the JSON settings file the launch passes with --settings, or to a new one when it passes none.

events.description: The runtime's hook event names to install the forwarder for, in the runtime's spelling.

stop.description: How the session stops the runtime, at a run's time limit or when Forager itself is stopped. Runtimes differ in what a signal means, one closes its session on SIGINT and drops it on SIGTERM, and this sets which the runtime gets. A run that sets a signal or a grace overrides it; absent, SIGTERM and ten seconds.

signal.description: The signal that requests the runtime's exit, among the ones the session sends.

grace.description: How long the runtime has after the signal before SIGKILL, as a duration: 30s.

headless.description: The arguments that mean the runtime runs without an interface. When one of them is among the arguments the runtime is started with, the session runs on pipes even at a terminal, exactly as when the caller requests pipes: the runtime is recorded as not interactive and the output source is read. Absent, the caller alone decides.

args.description: The arguments, each as the runtime spells it. A short one matches the whole token (-p); a long one matches the token or its --name=value form (--print, --print=...). Nothing else is inferred: a runtime that takes its prompt on standard input has no argument to list, and its caller sets headless itself.

secrets.description: The secrets the runtime needs and the variables it keeps for itself. runtimes.json lists the secrets of every descriptor the contract ships.

declares.description: The secrets the runtime reads, each from one variable, and where its value is set.

id.description: The declaration's id, unique among the declarations.

title.description: What the secret is, for a person choosing one.

name.description: The variable the runtime reads the secret from.

hosts.description: The hosts the value is set on: exact DNS names, no wildcard, no IP literal.

paths.description: The paths of those hosts the value is set on, in the policy's path grammar. Absent means every path.

auth.description: How the value is set on a request, a scheme from the closed set. A variable that is also a key's in model.keys has the same auth there.

one_of.description: Groups of declarations of which the runtime needs at most one, and exactly one of a required group. of lists declared ids, each id in at most one group; a declaration in no group is optional.

reserves.description: Variables the runtime reads a credential from beside the declared ones. Behind a wall, a declared or reserved variable that nothing sets, neither a placeholder, the run, the runtime's preparation, Forager nor the wall, is unset inside.

denies.description: Variables the session always leaves out of the server's set for the runtime, and reports: the ones that move where the runtime sends its requests and credentials, or change what it runs.

credential_files.description: Files in which the runtime keeps its credential, ~ being the home of the user Forager runs as.

model.description: The model API formats the runtime sends its requests in, where a composer writes a run's model id, effort value and model endpoint for the runtime, and the variables it reads a model key from. runtimes.json lists it for every descriptor that has one.

formats.description: The model API formats the runtime sends its requests in, each from api-format.schema.json.

model.description: Where the run's model id goes.

effort.description: Where an effort value goes, and the values the runtime accepts there. Absent, the runtime has no place for one.

run.description: Where the run's effort value goes.

agent.description: Where an agent's effort value goes, in the agent's file. Absent, the runtime has no place for an agent's effort.

endpoint.description: Where the base URL of the run's model API goes: always a variable.

variable.description: The variable the runtime reads the base URL from.

keys.description: The variables the runtime reads a model key from, one per API format and auth: the session gives an API credential's placeholder to the variable of the key whose format is the credential's and whose auth has the credential's scheme, the same header name, case ignored, and the same oauth. Each format is one of formats, each pair of format and auth appears once, and a variable is none of denies, overrides and the endpoint's variable.

format.description: The API format the key is for.

auth.description: How the runtime sends the key.

variable.description: The variable the runtime reads the key from.

overrides.description: The variables that would override the model id or effort value a composer writes. Behind a wall the session leaves each one's value out, of the server's, the run's, the machine's and the harness's values, the harness's computed values included, records it as denied, and unsets the name inside when nothing else sets it. Without a wall they change nothing.

rules.description: Evaluated in order against every record of the rule's source; the first rule whose match succeeds produces one event, and a record no rule matches produces nothing.

match.description: Every entry must match: a path into the record equals the value, a string, number or boolean; or, with {present: true}, the path exists. Nothing else: no patterns, no ranges, no expressions.

data.description: The event's data: each key is a field of the type's data, each value a dotted path into the record whose value is copied there unchanged. A path that does not exist leaves the field out.

place.description: Where a value goes, exactly one of: flag, an argument the runtime is started with, which takes the value; setting, a dotted key in the JSON settings file the launch passes; variable, an environment variable.

valued_place.description: A place, and in values the values the runtime accepts there.

agent_place.description: Where a value goes in an agent's file: frontmatter, a key of the file's frontmatter, and in values the values the runtime accepts there.

key_variable.description: A variable a runtime reads a key from: a variable's name other than HOME, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS and BASH_ENV, which change what runs. The schema refuses them in upper case; Forager refuses them in any letter case.
